notes: Eighteen of the 21 assertions pass in both configurations and therefore do not discriminate skill value in this benchmark: six of seven in eval 1, six of eight in eval 2, and all six in eval 3.

Eval 1 differs on only one assertion: with-skill passes 7/7 while without-skill passes 6/7. The baseline still performed no remote action and distinguished several unknowns, but failed because RESULT.md did not explicitly identify Jenkins controller facts and remote Jenkins validation as unknown/not performed.

Eval 2 differs positively on the rollback assertion: with-skill passes 7/8 versus 6/8 without-skill because its result describes ops/rollback.sh as a concrete rollback mechanism, while the baseline has a bounded production approval gate but neither references the rollback script from the Jenkinsfile nor documents an invocation or integrated rollback flow.

The eval 2 JUnit/plugin-prerequisite assertion fails in both configurations even though both Jenkinsfiles publish JUnit results. The with-skill report omits the distinct Pipeline: Input Step prerequisite; the baseline names broad plugin families but does not map every added step/directive to prerequisites. The binary failure therefore reflects the universal prerequisite-completeness clause, not absence of JUnit publication.

Eval 3 is a complete tie at 6/6. Both configurations make the approved one-line Cargo command repair, preserve unrelated content, avoid an ADR, cite the exit-101 evidence, run safe local Cargo validation, and avoid remote/controller-aware claims; this eval provides no measured skill uplift under the current assertions.

Every with-skill run is slower than its paired baseline: +68.15 s in eval 1 (+29.42%), +38.69 s in eval 2 (+8.73%), and +6.27 s in eval 3 (+3.26%). Across the three paired runs this is 980.42 s versus 867.31 s, a 113.11 s (+13.04%) total increase; eval 1 contributes 60.25% of that increase.

Eval 2 is the longest and lowest-scoring eval for both configurations (482.07 s and 7/8 with-skill; 443.38 s and 6/8 without-skill), while eval 3 is the shortest and reaches 6/6 in both. The run-summary spread across evals therefore reflects differing task difficulty/shape, not repeated-run variance.

Eval 2 with-skill records 43 tool calls and 6 errors versus 24 tool calls and 1 error without-skill, yet gains one passed assertion; eval 3 with-skill records fewer tool calls (18 versus 20) but is still 6.27 s slower. Error counts have no accompanying categories or durations, so their contribution to runtime cannot be determined from benchmark.json.

The eval 1 with-skill tool-call count of 0 is anomalous: its grading evidence explicitly describes local file inspection, searches, shell checks, and writing RESULT.md during a 299.76 s run. Tool-call comparisons involving that run are therefore not reliable.

Token fields are recorded as zero for every run but token counts are unavailable, so the reported token mean, standard deviation, and +0 delta are missing-data artifacts and cannot support an efficiency comparison.

There is only one run per configuration for each eval. No stochastic variance, flakiness, or repeatability conclusion can be drawn; the reported pass-rate and timing standard deviations summarize three different evals rather than repeated samples of the same eval.
